audit.report: The batch_replayable_inventory workload (pid 129874) entered an idle transaction that blocked checkout sessions, causing a 36% checkout success rate (35/108 failures) and approximately $5,963/min in revenue at risk. The database guardian identified the blocker as idle for 5.0s and confirmed termination would incur only a 4-minute replay cost due to the workload's idempotent, may_interrupt policy. The continuity guardian required change-calendar and protected-settlements evidence before approving termination; both invariants were satisfied, and the pact agreed to terminate in one round. The business recovered: all 36 checkouts succeeded (100%), lock waits cleared, and protected operations remained intact.
audit.root_cause: An idle batch_worker session (pid 129874) holding locks from a batch_replayable_inventory transaction blocked checkout sessions, degrading checkout success to 36% and putting ~$5,963/min of revenue at risk.
audit.negotiation_critique: The continuity guardian's first review (R1) correctly invoked invariants I2 and I3, prompting the database guardian to gather change-calendar and protected-settlements evidence; the second review (R2) was accepted immediately once both invariants were satisfied, so no guardian wasted a round.
follow_ups: Add batch_replayable_inventory to the change-calendar exclusion list so future termination proposals skip the change-calendar evidence step.
Instrument the batch_worker to surface idle-in-transaction duration in the lock graph metadata for faster trade-off probes.
Run a quarterly audit of protected-settlements status for batch workloads to ensure DB-2 evidence is always current.
